previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS involvement, was admitted for his 15th cycle of maintenance chemotherapy with high-dose methotrexate and rituximab. He reported feeling well with stable chronic floaters in his left eye and no new neurological or systemic symptoms. He received the planned chemotherapy with aggressive hydration and urinary alkalinization to prevent renal toxicity, given his history of methotrexate-induced acute tubular necrosis. Leucovorin rescue was initiated as his methotrexate level declined and continued until levels dropped below 0.1 µM. An MRI of the brain showed no evidence of lymphomatous recurrence and stable post-biopsy changes. A transient rise in liver enzymes and bilirubin was noted, possibly due to an interaction with home aspirin, which was held during admission and safely restarted at discharge. He tolerated treatment well, remained neurologically stable, and was discharged home in good condition with follow-up scheduled in six months.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  MRI brain with and without gadolinium.

INDICATION:  Lymphoma, undergoing chemotherapy.  Assess for disease
progression.

___ and ___ MRIs of the brain.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the brain was performed with and
without gadolinium as per departmental protocol.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of infarct, new mass or hemorrhage. 
Post-treatment changes include findings of left frontal biopsy with residual
mild FLAIR/T2 hyperintensity and T1 hypointensity within the subcortical white
matter and centrum semiovale in the posterior left frontal lobe.  Mild
residual adjacent susceptibility is also similar to prior.  Other chronic
findings include mild asymmetric prominence of the left lateral ventricle and
left greater than right paranasal sinus mucosal thickening.  There is no
abnormal enhancement.

IMPRESSION:
No evidence of new or recurrent disease.  Post-treatment changes in the left
frontal lobe are similar to prior.

HISTORY:  CNS lymphoma, question other organ involvement.

COMPARISON:  CT torso ___, other prior studies dating back to
___.

TECHNIQUE:  64-slice MDCT continuously acquired from the chest, abdomen and
pelvis.  After the administration of oral and 130 cc of IV contrast images
were displayed in multiple planes.

FINDINGS:  
CHEST WITH CONTRAST:  There are stable calcified nodules in the bilateral left
greater than right lung apices consistent with prior granulomatous infection. 
There are no additional nodules or consolidations or effusions.  There are
calcified subcarinal lymph nodes (2:27) consistent with prior infection or
treated lymphoma.  There is a central catheter tip with the tip terminating in
the SVC.  There is a focal coronary calcification in the mid LAD (2:33).  The
remainder of the heart and great vessels are normal.  There is no pathologic
mediastinal or axillary lymphadenopathy.

ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:  There are no suspicious liver lesions.  There is an
indeterminant stable hypodensity in the left lobe of liver which is too small
to characterize.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation. 
There is density within the fundus of the gallbladder consistent with
adenomyomatosis (2:70).  The pancreas and spleen are normal.  There is a tiny
hypodensity within the head of the pancreas which is too small to characterize
(2:69).  There is stable bulkiness of the left adrenal gland.  The kidneys
enhance and excrete contrast symmetrically.  There is a stable multilobulated
6 x 7 cm cystic lesion in the upper pole of the left kidney.  Differential
diagnosis includes chronically obstructed upper pole, obstructed upper pole
moiety, duplicated right renal collecting system or localized cystic disease
of the kidney.  No change in size or appearance since prior exam.  There is no
ascites or free abdominal air.  The aorta is of normal caliber throughout its
length.  There are aortic calcifications.

PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:  The small bowel is of normal caliber and appearance
throughout its length.  There is a 2.5-cm focal region of sigmoid thickening
(2:97).  This may represent artifact from peristalsis or true thickening. 
Remainder of the large bowel is normal.  The bladder is normal.  There are
scattered prostate calcifications.  There is no pelvic or inguinal
lymphadenopathy.  There is no free pelvic fluid.

There is a stable calcification within the right gluteal subcutaneous tissues.

BONE WINDOWS:  There are no lytic or sclerotic lesions.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of lymphoma involvement in the torso.
2.  Focal area of sigmoid wall thickening.  This may be an artifact related to
peristalsis; however, correlation should be made with any recent direct direct
visualization.

HISTORY:  ___ man, status post treatment for Hodgkin's/non-Hodgkin
lymphoma, now with severe headache.  Rule out intracranial hemorrhage.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior CT and MR with the latest CT on ___
and MRI on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast MDCT images were acquired through the head. 
Multiplanar reformatted images were obtained for evaluation.

FINDINGS:  There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, edema or
major vascular territorial infarct.  The known hypodensity along the left
superior frontal lobe is similar in appearance.  The ventricles and sulci are
normal in size and symmetric in configuration.  The gray-white matter
differentiation is well preserved.  Of note, there is a small ring-like
hyperdensity in the anterior left cerebellum abutting the fourth ventricle
(image 2:7), measures approximately 3 mm in diameter, of uncertain etiology,
may be an artifact.

The visualized paranasal sinuses are noted with scattered ethmoidal
opacifications.  The right mastoid air cells are clear.  The left mastoid air
cells are hypopneumatized.  There is no acute fracture.  A left frontal burr
hole is similar in appearance.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute intracranial pathological process.
2.  Similar appearance of post-treatment hypodensity in the left superior
frontal lobe.
